section_1.title: From ODEs to PDEs: A Visual Shift
section_1.content: Recall Ordinary Differential Equations (ODEs) where a function depends on one variable. Introduce PDEs as the language of multi-variable change. Use an animation showing a point moving along a line (ODE) versus a surface ripple (PDE).
section_1.example: A cat walking on a 1D path vs. a drop of water creating circular ripples on a 2D pond surface.

section_2.title: Defining the Operators
section_2.content: Introduce partial derivatives (∂/∂x, ∂/∂t) as 'looking' at change from specific directions. Use a 3D hill visualization where the slope is color-coded to show gradient changes along the X and Y axes independently.
section_2.example: A hiker measuring the steepness of a mountain slope facing North vs. the steepness facing East.

section_3.title: The Heat Equation: A Core PDE
section_3.content: Present the Heat Equation (ut = αuxx). Explain it as: 'the rate of change of temperature over time is proportional to the curvature of temperature in space.' Use a heatmap animation showing a hot iron rod cooling down.
section_3.example: An animation of a glowing-hot metal bar turning blue as it loses heat to the room, showing heat 'smoothing out' over time.

section_4.title: Boundary and Initial Conditions
section_4.content: Explain that PDEs need 'rules' to have a unique solution. Introduce Initial Conditions (the state at t=0) and Boundary Conditions (what happens at the edges). Use an animation of a vibrating guitar string held at both ends.
section_4.example: A guitar string: the 'Initial Condition' is the shape of the pluck; the 'Boundary Conditions' are the fixed ends at the nut and bridge.

section_5.title: Applications and Summary
section_5.content: Conclude by showcasing the ubiquity of PDEs in real life, from fluid dynamics to finance. Summarize the workflow: Model (PDE) -> Add Constraints (Boundaries) -> Solve.
section_5.example: A weather satellite map demonstrating how PDEs predict the movement of a hurricane by calculating pressure and wind velocity fields.

from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
